strengths: Novel theoretical framework with elegant bias-variance tradeoff characterization showing when PIDM outperforms BC through the lens of expected conditional action variance

Strong empirical validation of theoretical predictions: Figure 6-7 confirms gains concentrate in high-uncertainty regions, Figure 8 demonstrates predicted correlation between state predictor bias and performance

Rigorous experimental design with multiple environments: 2D navigation isolates efficiency gains from representation benefits, 3D game demonstrates real-world applicability (66% sample efficiency gain)

Exceptional experimental rigor with comprehensive appendices (180+ pages): hyperparameter searches, retrieval-based BC baseline, human/A* policy ablation to isolate bias effects, blind evaluation for 3D task

Clear presentation with logical progression from theory to experiments and honest discussion of limitations; extensive reproducibility details including hyperparameter configurations and multiple random seeds
weaknesses: Restrictive theoretical assumptions: Shared parameterization (Assumption 2) requiring BC as marginal of IDM is uncommon in practice; asymptotic analysis (Theorem 2-3) with finite-sample experiments lacks non-asymptotic bounds; MSE loss focus with only sketched extensions

Significant theory-practice gap on state predictors: Experiments use trivial predictors (nearest-neighbor lookup, random demo selection) while modern PIDM uses diffusion/video models; theory assumes fixed predictor but recent work jointly trains components

Incomplete practical characterization: Theorem 3 condition (13) is complex and difficult to verify from data; simplified version (14) requires strong asymptotic unbiasedness; no guidance for practitioners on when conditions hold

Limited scope of complex environments: Only one 3D task evaluated (Tour in Bleeding Edge) versus four 2D tasks; state predictor in 3D is intentionally trivial (random selection), not representative of real-world sophistication; would benefit from 2-3 additional complex tasks

Assumption 3 (regularity conditions) imposes strong technical requirements on Fisher information and differentiability that may not hold for modern architectures; Assumption 4 lacks clear intuition for when approximate state predictor places mass on informative states

Potential fairness concerns in baseline comparison: BC required different learning rate schedules and was less stable (Table 6), raising questions about experimental parity despite hyperparameter search

strengths: Clear and elegant theoretical result (Theorem 1) characterizing the performance gap as conditional action variance, providing new interpretation for known empirical phenomenon
Realistic analysis of non-optimal estimators (Corollary 1) that identifies the key tradeoff: variance reduction from conditioning versus bias/variance from covariate shift

Strong empirical validation directly testing theoretical predictions: Section 5.3 shows IDM attends to future states precisely where Δ(s) is large (Figure 7), Section 5.4 demonstrates covariate shift effects with controlled experiments

Comprehensive experiments with rigorous methodology: careful hyperparameter tuning, proper baselines including retrieval-based BC variant, extensive ablations in appendices, statistical significance testing
Excellent presentation quality with clear motivation, informative figures, logical flow, and honest discussion of assumptions and limitations
Thorough reproducibility support through code availability promise and detailed appendices with environment specifications, hyperparameters, and implementation details
weaknesses: Restrictive theoretical assumptions (especially Assumption 3 on correct specification) not fully addressed; limited discussion of when they might be violated in practice

Theory requires 'sufficiently large n and m' but experiments demonstrate gains in small-data regime (5-30 demonstrations); gap between asymptotic theory and finite-sample practice not rigorously bridged
Limited characterization of when PIDM wins beyond empirical observations; no principled method to predict which domains benefit from decomposition, reducing practical predictive power
Complex sample efficiency analysis (Theorem 2 with Corollary 2) relies on restrictive conditions like equal bias/derivatives between BC and IDM that may not hold in practice
Limited empirical novelty: validates existing observations from prior work (Du et al. 2023, Tian et al. 2025) rather than enabling new algorithmic improvements or surprising discoveries

Simple experimental setup with relatively simple 2D navigation tasks and instance-based state predictor differing substantially from modern approaches (diffusion/transformers) used in cited prior work
Incomplete statistical testing for 2D experiments (no formal significance across tasks) and fewer random seeds for 3D experiments (5 vs. 20 for 2D)
Brief treatment of extensions to broader settings (cross-entropy loss, non-i.i.d. sampling in appendices) acknowledged as needing 'formal treatment'
